entry.title: Brazil’s Economic Impasse
entry.summary:
Monica de Bolle, an expert in Brazilian economic policy, makes an authoritative argument that Brazil’s economic problems will persist no matter the outcome of the country’s presidential election. A Flávio Bolsonaro administration would fare no better than Lula when it comes to reducing debt and delivering growth—and Bolsonaro’s illiberal policies could make the economic picture even worse.

Source: Foreign Affairs · Tags: #geopolitics #defense-strategy

entry.title: A Less-Is-More Strategy for America. Barry Posen, a professor at MIT, is one of America's leading experts on international security.
entry.summary:
Barry Posen, a professor at MIT, is one of America's leading experts on international security. He argues that the United States military is breaking down because it has been overused and overextended over the last 30 years, and that the only way to repair it is for Washington to exercise much more restraint.

Source: Foreign Affairs · Tags: #geopolitics #defense-strategy

entry.title: The Chokepoint Trap
entry.summary:
Niall Ferguson, the leading historian of empire, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and AI scholar Lisa Klassen offer a novel reframing of the US-China AI race in the history of world empires. The authors argue that AI is inherently imperial in it ambitions and structure, and that, like previous technological empires, China and US have amassed extraordinary global but that it's happening at a much faster pace. Rise and fall cycle will be faster.

entry.title: The Limits of American Power
entry.summary:
William McRaven, a retired four-star admiral and a major figure in American military affairs, uses history and his personal experiences to make an authoritative case that American leaders frequently overestimate the potential of military force to achieve political ends—and that new technologies like AI will exacerbate this problem.

Source: Foreign Affairs · Tags: #geopolitics #defense-strategy

entry.title: The Fog of Tech
entry.summary:
Mara Karlin, a defense policy expert who served as senior national-security official in multiple American administrations, makes an authoritative case that war planners tend to be overconfident about their ability to predict how new tools will shape the battlefield—blinding them to the unchanging realities of war. Source: Foreign Affairs · Tags: #geopolitics #defense-strategy

entry.title: Empires of AI
entry.summary:
In this essay, Niall Ferguson, one of the world’s foremost experts on imperial history, teams up the former CEO of Google, Eric Schmidt, and the researcher Lisa Klaassen to make the provocative argument that AI is an inherently “imperial technology”—and to reveal what the fate of past empires might say about the future of U.S.-Chinese competition in a world shaped by AI.

Source: Foreign Affairs · Tags: #geopolitics #defense-strategy

entry.title: AI Is a Choice
entry.summary:
Alex Imas, Mohamed El-Erian, and James Manyika, leading voices at the intersection of business and technology, argue that realizing AI’s potential requires giving workers, communities, AI labs, infrastructure developers, and big companies a share of the gains. Using insights from game theory, they argue that increased cooperation can make AI work for all.

Source: Foreign Affairs · Tags: #geopolitics #defense-strategy

entry.title: The China Price. In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S.
entry.summary:
In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate.

Source: Foreign Affairs · Tags: #geopolitics #defense-strategy
